VERIFIED: The offline observation analyzer reproduces every stored ratio, failure count, longest gap, processing p95, sync verdict, evidence status, and overall verdict for all three retained sessions.
Every retained observation failure is classified as candidates_rejected rather than read failure or no_markers.
Every failure frame entered the expensive ROI miss, preprocessing, and full-frame fallback path.
The first session observed 76 rejected frames but saved zero representative frames because three cv2.imencode calls returned false.
The current capture source labels that encode failure as cv2.imwrite returned false even though the implementation calls cv2.imencode at tools/camera_toolchain/capture_sync_run.py:365-371.
INFERENCE: The observation bottleneck is likely a combination of view-dependent target quality and the expensive fallback path; the saved thumbnails show the vehicle and printed tag, but they do not prove that the target quadrilateral was valid enough for the detector.
The 1080p detector workload is a real contributor to processing latency on rejected frames, but latency alone is not proven to be the primary cause of candidate rejection.
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: The exact candidate rejection cause is not recoverable for the first session because its representative failure thumbnails were not saved.
The retained diagnostics do not expose per-candidate rejection reasons or corner geometry, so detector thresholds cannot be justified for change from these artifacts alone.
No observation-gate pass, continuous AprilTag track, validated 1080p ground homography, or real algorithm improvement is established.

decision.next_offline_action: Harden and instrument failure-frame encoding diagnostics before requesting a matched real rerun; keep detector thresholds, calibration, firmware, and control unchanged.
